By: S. H. Pious, Senior Correspondent, The Daily Hallelujah

In an unprecedented act of ecclesiastical injustice, Reverend Bartholomew “Barty” Pearlyton of First Pentecostal Praise & Purge Ministries has filed a formal blasphemy complaint against local mail carrier Gary “G-man” Wiggins, alleging “violation of divine protocol” after delivering a 20-pound bag of household trash to his front step—labeled, in permanent marker, “BIBLE OF THE CHURCH OF ATEISM: HONOR THY INPUT.”

“I felt the Holy Spirit tremble,” Reverend Pearlyton reported, clutching ajar of holy basil oil. “The bag had a doodle of a lion with a halo… eating a communion wafer! Three of the cans were labeled ‘Jesus’ Lube’—a clear attempt to spiritually destabilize the faithful!”

The “Bible” in question was, in fact, a recycling bin left by a teenager after a zine-making class. The “lion eating a wafer” was a scribbled doodle of a cat. “Jesus’ Lube” was a defunct brand of olive oil Gary had misread as “Jesus’ Lube” due to blurry handwriting. G-man, a retired librarian and WWII vet, responded with polite confusion: “Look, I deliver mail. I don’t write theology. And if I knew someone was gonna sue me for recycling… I’d’ve used bubble wrap.”

The church is now demanding a public apology, a new van painted with the “10 Commandments of Mail Sortation,” and a week of free free-range quail (a divine provision, per Leviticus 11:16—allegedly, if you squint).

“This is not about trash,” said Reverend Pearlyton. “It’s about the sanctity of our sacred brand assets. Gmail has email filters. We need Divinity Filters.”

Local atheist and law professor Dr. Lena Wu, who was not involved in the incident but was probably holding her head right now, stated: “We already have fraud, trespass, and slander laws. We don’t need legal mysteries where trash becomes a theological trial. Frankly, if your faith can be intimidated by a bag labeled ‘Bible of the Church of Ateism,’ maybe you’re not as holy as you think.”

The case has sparked national outrage—not from atheists, but from accountants. “If we start litigating every Kraft Macaroni & Cheese box with ‘Hallelujah’ on the side,” said one CPA, “we’re going to have to charge churches for every slurpy sound effect in worship songs.”

The court hearing is scheduled for next Tuesday. The judge, a devout Methodist who recently had his own emotional breakdown when a barista mispronounced his name, has already requested the district’s entire collection of church-shaped stickers to “inspect for impropriety.”

[Final note: Gary Wiggins has since been offered a job as “Spiritual Compliance Officer” at Applebee’s, where he will now be trained to recognize sacred consumer goods before delivery.]
